clue.text: Large meal European tucked into quickly

indicators.note: something tucked into another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: fast means quickly
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe wolfs down a big dinner in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a lavish, plentiful meal, so the noun phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Blooming fine cow in centre of Margate

indicators.note: the centre is the middle, so only the middle letter of the town's name is kept

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a lower is one that lows, as a cow does
taken as written
the middle letter of the seven-letter Margate

explanation.surface: A splendid cow turns up in the middle of a Kent seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is an English seaside resort. A cow lows (moos), so it is a 'lower', rhyming with mower.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooming means producing flowers, and flowering is the same participle in another word.

clue.text: Prevent State Department's termination

indicators.note: termination is the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
last letter of Department

explanation.surface: A call to block the State Department from being shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State Department' looks like the US ministry; split it into a verb and a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to prevent it happening, a synonym.

clue.text: Guy gets 50 per cent off cups and saucers?

indicators.note: half taken off means removing half of the word's letters

blocks.note: to guy is to mock or tease
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man picks up crockery in a half-price sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy is a verb here: to ridicule. The question mark shows cups and saucers are an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea sets are matching crockery collections that typically include cups and saucers.

clue.text: What satisfied customer would do this?

blocks.note: first meaning: an exclamation asking someone to repeat themselves
second meaning: return to a shop or restaurant for more

explanation.walkthrough: 'What' reads as the start of a question, but it is a definition on its own: the spoken request to repeat something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a colloquial request for repetition, like 'pardon?', and a description of a happy patron returning.

clue.text: Edward supports child I had told off

blocks.note: ch is the abbreviation for child
I'd is the contraction of I had
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward backs up a child who admits being reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supports' puts the first piece underneath the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told off is to be scolded, and chided is the past tense for that rebuke.

clue.text: One engaged by church?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone betrothed in a church wedding
setter's reading: employed, as a member of the clergy is hired by a church

explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests a couple marrying, but here it means taken on as an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman serving a congregation is employed by the church, so he is one the church has engaged.

clue.text: Claims benefits without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: assets are benefits or advantages
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone takes welfare payments without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but the setter uses the older sense, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Claims as a verb means states as true, and asserts is the same, a synonym.

clue.text: Saw around five American books generating profit

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the saying encloses the other pieces

blocks.note: a saw is an old saying, an adage
V is the Roman numeral five
A is the abbreviation for American
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A carpenter cuts through several US books to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the tool or a past tense, but it is a noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit as a noun means gain or benefit, and an advantage is a benefit gained.

clue.text: Sister swapping uniform with old Scandinavian

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means a letter is exchanged for a different one

blocks.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A nurse changes out of her uniform alongside an ageing Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapping uniform with old' means the U is replaced by O; 'old' looks like part of the definition but supplies the new letter. Sister is the British title for a senior ward nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse is an adjective for the people and languages of Scandinavia, especially in its medieval form.

clue.text: Aida perhaps not reflecting about current surgical procedure

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the word is read backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: Aida is an opera by Verdi
the word not, read backwards
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A staging of Verdi's opera is likened, oddly, to a medical operation done backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Aida as one example of the category. The reversed word wraps around the current symbol before following the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a surgical procedure performed on a patient, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Boats ultimately always dock

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: last letter of Boats
ever means always

explanation.surface: Boats in the end always tie up at the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like a harbour noun, but it is the verb meaning to cut off, as with docking a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to cut short or remove, and to sever is to cut off, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Great old US band hugged by teen, oddly

indicators.note: something hugged by another is held inside its arms, so it sits within
oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: ex means former or old
first and third letters of teen
R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: A teenager clings to a vintage American group in a fan's embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of very large in degree, as in great or extreme danger, is synonymous here.

clue.text: Weird stone assortment

blocks.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
a range is an assortment or variety

explanation.surface: An odd collection of rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone here is the British unit of weight, fourteen pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and strange are adjectives meaning odd or unusual, plain synonyms.

clue.text: Take a firm stand in street following Starmer's incompetence, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of the two words is kept
following places the street abbreviation after the initials, so it comes second in the chain

blocks.note: taken as written
first letters of Starmer's and incompetence
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone digs in on a street protest after the Prime Minister's blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is a UK Prime Minister. 'Following' places the street abbreviation after the two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to hold firmly to a position and refuse to yield, an idiom-level synonym.

clue.text: Adult enthralled by scariest cuckoo's flight

indicators.note: something enthralled by another is held captive inside it
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film certificates

explanation.surface: A grown-up is gripped by the most frightening bird's escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo's flight' suggests a bird flying, but cuckoo means mad and flight is a set of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a staircase, so the noun is a synonym in that architectural sense.

clue.text: Convince doctor he's a prude, leaving hospital

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone tries to talk a medic into accepting that a man is prudish and should be discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun for a medic but is a verb meaning tamper with. Remove the H, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone is to convince them by argument, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Considered mate's diet unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regards a friend's eating habits as odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered, as in judged or reckoned, matches estimated in the sense of an approximate assessment.

clue.text: Star once playing grandfather, maybe

indicators.note: playing suggests letters at play, moving about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former celebrity actor takes on the role of an old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is one example of a forebear in the family line, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Good boy studies, getting cheers

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lad is a boy
dens are private studies, rooms for reading

explanation.surface: A well-behaved boy earns applause for his schoolwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a noun for applause, but it is the verb meaning makes happy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to lift their spirits, which is exactly what gladdens means.

clue.text: German article's covering upsetting fight for boxers?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads bottom to top
covering means wrapped over, so the article's letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: der is a German definite article, plus the s
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: A German newspaper piece covers an upsetting boxing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters, chiming with the fight, but it means boxer shorts; drawers is an old word for underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers are a kind of men's underpants, and drawers is the older general word for underpants.

clue.text: Focus attention on Cockney?

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to emphasise or highlight
second meaning: the way of speaking of East Londoners, an example of a regional pronunciation

explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class dialect of East London; the question mark flags it as one example of the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning emphasise and a noun for a distinctive regional pronunciation, of which Cockney is a case.

clue.text: Wealthy man endlessly angry about rising employment

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: cross means angry
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A rich man is furious at growing unemployment, or at least the employment figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Croesus was a king of ancient Lydia famed for his riches, hence 'as rich as Croesus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus is the proverbial byword for great wealth, so he is the archetypal wealthy man.

clue.text: Fruit blocking ship's weapons

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so one piece is lodged within the other

blocks.note: SS is steamship, plus the s
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A cargo of fruit is clogging up a warship's armoury.
explanation.definitionFit: Spears are long pointed throwing or thrusting weapons, an example of the class.

clue.text: Top on Parisian female? Wonderful!

blocks.note: sur is French for on
F is the abbreviation for female
ace means excellent, wonderful

explanation.surface: Someone admires a stylish blouse on a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' tells you to put on into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface of something is its top or outermost layer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Leave city in Croatia

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang verb, to depart quickly
second meaning: a port city on the Dalmatian coast

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a travel instruction; 'leave' is the informal verb 'to split'.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is slang for departing, and Split is Croatia's second-largest city on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Stumbling-block for this writer with large book sent back

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
the setter refers to themselves
L is the abbreviation for large
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A writer finds a big book an obstacle and returns it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumbling-block is an obstacle or difficulty, which is what a problem is.

clue.text: John almost set free

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
taken as written

explanation.surface: John has nearly been released from custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is slang for a lavatory; loo is the British word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Free as an adjective means unconfined, and loose means not tied up or held, a synonym.

clue.text: Let student rest

blocks.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A command to allow a pupil some downtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like 'allow', but it is the verb meaning rent out. British learner drivers display an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to rent it out, which is what leasing it means.

clue.text: Perhaps ferry entrance

blocks.note: first meaning: a means of carrying people, of which a ferry is an example
second meaning: a verb, to fill with delight, stressed on the second syllable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb en-TRANCE, to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is one form of conveyance, and to entrance someone is to carry them away with delight, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Criminal rates pinching certain valuable objects

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or corrupt, so the letters are bent out of order
pinching means grabbing and holding, so one piece is gripped inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Extortionate charges are a way of stealing people's precious possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasures are prized, valuable possessions, a direct synonym for the plural noun phrase.

clue.text: Golfer is in demand on a regular basis

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A golfer is constantly sought after.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Snead was a famous American golfer of the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Snead was a champion professional player, so the name fits as an example of a golfer.
